dedupe_keys.name: puerto rico after hurricanes irma and maria damage to health and social services and courses of action for recovery rand hsoac

description: This case study is RAND's assessment of Puerto Rico's health and social services before and after Hurricanes Irma and Maria struck in September 2017, prepared to support the government of Puerto Rico's long-term recovery plan. It was produced by the Homeland Security Operational Analysis Center, a federally funded research and development centre operated by RAND, and published as a free research report. The report describes predisaster conditions, including chronic disease rates above US averages, emigration that shrank the workforce and tax base, and weak fiscal transparency; documents hurricane damage, where damage to buildings and to electrical, water and communications infrastructure closed clinical and diagnostic facilities, some for several months, and open facilities suffered intermittent power and water, lost access to records and limited staff; and sets out 31 courses of action. Coverage is the whole island. The report and summary are free to download as PDF from RAND, under RAND copyright. Caveats: it is a qualitative damage and needs assessment, not a quantitative model, and later recovery progress is outside its scope. Its courses of action fall under four themes: building system capacity for disasters and routine times, strengthening the health and social services workforce, supporting at-need populations, and creating health-promoting communities. Simulation uses: a reference for healthcare interdependency and cascading failure scenarios with power and water outages, and for recovery and resilience planning. Related records: the Puerto Rico Maria and 2020 earthquakes reconnaissance (case_study-puerto-rico-maria-2020-earthquakes-multihazard-reconnaissance) and the PR100 grid resilience study (case_study-puerto-rico-grid-resilience-and-transitions-to-100-renewable-energy-study-pr100).
